note_tweet.text:
I’m a big-time pandal hopper. Durga Puja evenings are something I look forward to every year. ❤️

Today, I got ready and stepped out to visit Ahiritola, Kumartuli, Chorbagan, Chaltabagan and other nearby pandals.

After visiting just two pujas, it started raining. I took a cab back home. When we passed near Chorbagan’s main entrance, I saw police personnel and civic volunteers. The rain had kept the crowd relatively thin, and for a moment, I thought of going back.

But with the rain and the difficulty of finding a cab, I decided to return home.

And then I saw the news.

Completely shattered. Heartbroken. Unable to process what happened.

I keep thinking… if it hadn’t rained, would I have still been there? Would I have been standing among those people?

There are so many thoughts running through my mind. So many unanswered questions. A strange, unsettling void that’s difficult to explain.

We go out to celebrate Maa Durga, to seek blessings, to create memories with our loved ones. Nobody steps out expecting that a festive evening could turn into their last.

People getting injured is heartbreaking enough. Losing lives while visiting a Durga Puja pandal is simply too devastating to comprehend.

Life is frighteningly unpredictable. Sometimes, a little rain, a delayed cab, or a small decision to return home can change everything.

Tonight, my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one and to everyone affected by this tragedy.

May they find the strength to endure this unimaginable pain. 🙏

Some festive evenings leave us with memories. Others leave us questioning how fragile life really is.

Om Shanti. 🙏
